dct_description_sm: The main objective of the Arctic SOLAS programme was to determine how variability in sea ice and water masses in the Arctic influences the ocean-ice-atmosphere exchanges of climate-active gases and particles and the chemical and radiative properties of the Arctic atmosphere. In this context, the 2008 N2O project performed what we believe to be the first-ever measurements of N2O within the sea ice matrix. The objective was to determine whether the sea ice is a source or a sink of N2O to the atmosphere. Other authors have observed enrichments of other gases in sea ice, and the rich microbial community including ice algae and associated bacteria may support high N2O production rates.
dct_title_s: Arctic SOLAS 2008 nitrous oxide (N2O) in sea ice
